name: Siren
description: The Siren: armed and disarmed from Insteon controllers, it sounds a siren or chime when a linked sensor or controller triggers it.

operatingFlags.name: programmingLock
operatingFlags.label: Programming lock
operatingFlags.description: The SET button can't be used for linking.

operatingFlags.name: blinkOnTraffic
operatingFlags.label: Blink LED on traffic
operatingFlags.description: The LED blinks whenever the siren hears Insteon traffic, which may be a message it repeats.

verification.note: The Siren Module Developer Notes' operating flags chart makes 0 on and 1 off; their property table, used here, makes 1 on.

operatingFlags.name: disarmed
operatingFlags.label: Disarmed
operatingFlags.description: The siren is disarmed. The arm command clears it.

verification.note: One example in the Siren Module Developer Notes reads bit 2 set as armed; their chart and property table, used here, make it disarmed.

operatingFlags.name: memoryFull
operatingFlags.label: Database full
operatingFlags.description: The last add or modify of an ALL-Link database record failed because the database is full. It clears when the siren powers up.

verification.note: The Siren Module Developer Notes' operating flags chart lists bit 3 as no data; their property table, used here, makes it database full.

operatingFlags.name: cleanupReport
operatingFlags.label: Send cleanup reports
operatingFlags.description: The siren sends a cleanup report after each group command it sends. Set by default.

operatingFlags.name: hopPowerlineOnRadio
operatingFlags.label: Repeat powerline over radio
operatingFlags.description: The siren repeats every powerline message over RF, whatever its hop count, which can cause collisions. Clear, it repeats only messages it heard first over the powerline.

values.name: alertType
values.label: Alert sound
values.description: The sound an alert makes: 0x00 a chime, 0x01 a siren.

values.name: delayAndDuration
values.label: Delay and duration
values.description: Bit 7 and the duration in bits 0 through 6, 0 to 127, roughly in seconds. For an alert, bit 7 delays sounding by 30 seconds; for arming, it makes the 45-second countdown silent.

verification.note: The Siren Module Developer Notes' tap-tap example writes 0x80 to make the arming countdown audible, the opposite of their property table, used here; they give the duration as 1 to 120 seconds in one place and 0 to 127 in others.

writes.name: alertType
writes.description: Sets the alert type. Linking copies it into the new responder record.

writes.name: delayAndDuration
writes.description: Sets the delay and duration, or the arming countdown. Linking copies it into the new responder record.

standardCommands.name: soundAlert
standardCommands.description: Sounds the alert, armed or not, at once or after the delay its cmd2 sets.

parameter.name: delayAndDuration
parameter.description: Bit 7 and the duration in bits 0 through 6, 0 to 127, roughly in seconds. For an alert, bit 7 delays sounding by 30 seconds; for arming, it makes the 45-second countdown silent.

standardCommands.name: readStatus
standardCommands.description: Reads how long the alert has left to sound. The acknowledgment's cmd1 carries the ALL-Link database delta.

reply.name: secondsLeft
reply.description: About how many seconds the alert has left, or 0 when it isn't sounding.

verification.note: The Siren Module Developer Notes also list armed states in this reply: 0x00 disarmed, 0x01 armed home, 0x03 armed away and 0x04 both. The catalog reads it as the seconds left, as the notes' example and later 0x19 03 command do.

standardCommands.name: readArmedState
standardCommands.description: Reads whether the siren is armed or arming, in which modes, and how long the arming countdown has left. The acknowledgment's cmd1 is 0x19.

reply.name: armedState
reply.description: Bits 6 and 7 give the modes the siren is armed or arming in, and bits 0 through 5 the seconds left of the arming countdown.

bits.name: home
bits.description: Armed or arming in home mode.

bits.name: away
bits.description: Armed or arming in away mode.

verification.note: The Siren Module Developer Notes' property table gives the countdown as bits 0 through 6; their 0x19 03 command, used here, gives bits 0 through 5.

extendedCommands.name: arm
extendedCommands.description: Arms the siren at once, with no countdown.

verification.note: The Siren Module Developer Notes don't give the mode values; their example arms with 0x01.

notes: Responder groups 1, 3 and 5 trigger the alert when the siren is armed away, home or either; groups 2, 4 and 6 arm it away, home or both. A group On (cmd1 0x11) to an arm group starts a 45-second countdown, which beeps each second unless the link makes it silent, Fast On (cmd1 0x12) starts it silently, and another arm group during the countdown changes the mode without restarting it. A group Off (cmd1 0x13) to any arm group disarms the siren and silences it. The Siren Module Developer Notes' description of arming says Fast Off arms silently; their group commands and the Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual give Fast On.
While it's arming, linked devices don't trigger the alert. Sending the arm group again, or Off, cancels arming.
While the alert sounds, the siren broadcasts Fast On and Fast Off (cmd1 0x12 and 0x14) to group 1 in turn, every 2 seconds.

An alert record's data holds the delay and duration, the alert type and a record type; an arm record's data holds a record type. The Siren Module Developer Notes also say linking to an arm group stores the countdown behavior.
The siren adds or modifies a record with ALL-Link database command D2 0x03, matching on group and ID, and answers 0x2F with NAK 0xF9 when its database is full.
